summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

Primary endpoint: Predicted oxidation stability error [h]. Comparator: Arrhenius or established chemical-kinetics stability model with independent chromatographic oxidation-product measurements. Strong rival: apparent stability from evaporation losses, photobleaching, unmeasured hydroperoxide products, packaging absorption or censored aging times. Withheld intervention: blind oxygen/headspace and wavelength-filter shift paired with dark controls. Independent observation: external aged-mixture concentration/time series with certified oxidation-product identities and conservative uncertainty. Binding stop: unquantified oxidation products, unsafe peroxide formation, unmatched light spectrum, unclear thermal exposure or unreported censored samples. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F135 · Synthetic Feasibility of Computationally Designed Aroma Molecules at the Limit Scientific object: route-level feasibility of algorithmically proposed odorant molecules without claiming experimental synthesis. Physical basis: retrosynthesis route connectivity, available starting materials, stereochemical control, protecting group compatibility, yield uncertainty, cost and independent medicinal-chemistry review. Primary endpoint: Synthesizable valid candidate fraction [%]. Comparator: commercially available natural analogues, expert route review and classical template retrosynthesis at matched candidate count. Strong rival: unavailable precursors, circular retrosynthesis, imaginary reaction templates, unresolved stereochemistry, omitted hazardous steps or selective reporting. Withheld intervention: sealed stockout of a required precursor and strict reaction-template embargo. Independent observation: independent chemist review of non-operational route plausibility, lawful precursor availability and all rejected molecular identities. Binding stop: route not independently verifiable, unavailable or restricted starting material, hazardous reaction proposal, unsafe waste stream or missing full denominator. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. THIRTY DIMENSIONED CANDIDATE FORMULAS F131 / RELATION 1: Graph validity rate. Formula V=100*N_valid/N_generated. Dimensional condition: N counts of all generated chemical graphs; V percent, failed parsing included. Predicted geometric signature: Validity plateau across sampling temperature and novelty share. Rival: A parser-specific sanitization definition may change the counted graph identity.. F131 / RELATION 2: Canonical uniqueness. Formula U=100*N_distinct_valid/N_valid. Dimensional condition: Counts of canonical graphs; percentage, include stereochemical identity policy. Predicted geometric signature: Duplicate basin at low sampling entropy. Rival: Canonicalization mismatch can falsely increase molecular diversity.. F131 / RELATION 3: Novel scaffold share. Formula N=100*N_novel_scaffolds/N_valid. Dimensional condition: Novel scaffold count divided by valid generated count, percent. Predicted geometric signature: Scaffold novelty ridge at constrained validity. Rival: Training corpus incompleteness may imitate novelty.. F131 / RELATION 4: Penalized graph objective. Formula J=log(p_graph)-lambda*P_invalid. Dimensional condition: Log probability and penalty dimensionless, lambda dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Feasible manifold under valence penalties. Rival: Reward hacking can improve J while molecular chemistry degrades.. F131 / RELATION 5: Shannon graph diversity. Formula H=-sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Dimensional condition: p_i relative graph frequencies; entropy nats. Predicted geometric signature: Diversity ridge subject to sampling noise. Rival: A high-entropy distribution can be mostly chemically invalid.. F131 / RELATION 6: Held-out validity difference. Formula DeltaV=V_model-V_classical. Dimensional condition: Both V in percent; DeltaV percentage points. Predicted geometric signature: External scaffold frontier can invert an internal advantage. Rival: A strong classic fragment generator may beat the proposed model.. F132 / RELATION 1: Blind attribute correlation. Formula r=cov(yhat,y)/(sd(yhat)*sd(y)). Dimensional condition: Standard deviation and covariance matched scale; r dimensionless from -1 to 1. Predicted geometric signature: Correlation saddle under rater reliability and scaffold shift. Rival: Repeated ratings or leaked descriptors can inflate correlation.. F132 / RELATION 2: Correlation Fisher transform. Formula z=0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)). Dimensional condition: r dimensionless -1<r<1; z dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Exploding endpoints near perfect correlation. Rival: High z is unstable for small or dependent test sets.. F132 / RELATION 3: Attribute MAE. Formula MAE=(1/N)*sum|yhat_i-y_i|. Dimensional condition: Predictions and ratings in same registered rating-scale units. Predicted geometric signature: Error valley across label calibration. Rival: A changed rater scale can fabricate gains.. F132 / RELATION 4: Hierarchical rater variance. Formula u_total2=u_molecule2+u_rater2+u_lab2. Dimensional condition: All variances in squared descriptor rating units. Predicted geometric signature: Uncertainty floor across cohorts. Rival: Ignoring correlated raters invalidates independence.. F132 / RELATION 5: Rank-based agreement. Formula rho=1-6*sum_i d_i^2/(N*(N^2-1)). Dimensional condition: Spearman rho dimensionless for uncensored tie-free ranks. Predicted geometric signature: Ranking plateau despite poor absolute prediction. Rival: Ties and censoring require rank correction.. F132 / RELATION 6: Group parity difference. Formula Delta_r=max_g(r_g)-min_g(r_g). Dimensional condition: Each r dimensionless, Delta dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Cross-chemotype fairness ridge. Rival: Small groups yield noisy extreme correlations.. F133 / RELATION 1: Pareto nondominated count. Formula N_P=number_of_feasible_nondominated_molecules. Dimensional condition: Count of identity-unique structures; all hard constraints held fixed. Predicted geometric signature: Pareto boundary shaped by volatility and hazard penalties. Rival: Predictor uncertainty can alter dominance order.. F133 / RELATION 2: Antoine vapour relation. Formula log10(P)=A-B/(C+T). Dimensional condition: A dimensionless, B and C in same temperature units as T; P in declared reference pressure units. Predicted geometric signature: Volatility-temperature curvature. Rival: Antoine parameters cannot be transferred outside calibrated range.. F133 / RELATION 3: Constraint feasibility fraction. Formula F=100*N_feasible/N_generated. Dimensional condition: Both counts; F percent for full proposal ledger. Predicted geometric signature: Feasibility cliff near safety thresholds. Rival: Missing toxicity alerts systematically overestimate feasibility.. F133 / RELATION 4: Hypervolume improvement. Formula DeltaHV=HV(Pareto)-HV(baseline). Dimensional condition: Both HV in product of normalized objective units, dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Pareto knee surface. Rival: Reference point changes can reverse winner.. F133 / RELATION 5: Expected risk penalty. Formula R=Sum_j p_j*c_j. Dimensional condition: p_j probability, c_j dimensionless normalized consequence; R dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Safety risk valley. Rival: Alert probabilities lacking validation do not equal hazard probability.. F133 / RELATION 6: Robust dominance criterion. Formula D=I[f1>=f1_ref+u1 and f2>=f2_ref+u2]. Dimensional condition: All objectives and uncertainties in matched normalized units; D binary. Predicted geometric signature: Uncertainty band separates stable from fragile fronts. Rival: Overconfident surrogate prediction biases nondominated count.. F134 / RELATION 1: Stability time absolute error. Formula MAE_t=mean(abs(t_pred-t_ref)). Dimensional condition: t_pred, t_ref in h; MAE h, include censored handling. Predicted geometric signature: Time-error basin with oxygen and light. Rival: Evaporation can mimic decay-time predictions.. F134 / RELATION 2: Pseudo-first-order oxidation. Formula C(t)=C0*exp(-k*t). Dimensional condition: C mass/volume; t h; k h^-1. Predicted geometric signature: Monotone exponential slope. Rival: Competing radical branches violate first-order assumption.. F134 / RELATION 3: Oxidation half-life. Formula t_half=ln(2)/k. Dimensional condition: k h^-1; time h. Predicted geometric signature: Half-life ridge in photon intensity. Rival: Photochemistry and oxygen supply may change k through time.. F134 / RELATION 4: Arrhenius rate law. Formula k(T)=A*exp(-Ea/(R*T)). Dimensional condition: k and A h^-1; Ea J/mol; R J/(mol*K); T K. Predicted geometric signature: Temperature acceleration saddle. Rival: Extrapolation across phase changes is invalid.. F134 / RELATION 5: Photooxidation product yield. Formula Y=100*m_products/m_start. Dimensional condition: Both masses same units; Y percent, specify chemical product coverage. Predicted geometric signature: Mass-balance deficit ridge. Rival: Unmeasured volatile byproducts break closure.. F134 / RELATION 6: Reaction-pathway sum. Formula k_total=sum_j k_j. Dimensional condition: Each branch rate h^-1 under common kinetics. Predicted geometric signature: Competing branch rate landscape. Rival: A missing branch falsifies inferred single-rate stability.. F135 / RELATION 1: Validated route fraction. Formula S=100*N_route_verified/N_generated. Dimensional condition: Counts include all invalid/unroutable candidates; percent. Predicted geometric signature: Route feasibility cliff with step count. Rival: Automatic retrosynthesis is not confirmed synthesis.. F135 / RELATION 2: Route yield product. Formula Y_route=prod_i y_i. Dimensional condition: Each step yield y_i dimensionless 0..1, route total fraction. Predicted geometric signature: Compounding yield decay frontier. Rival: Step yields from unrelated chemistry cannot be multiplied blindly.. F135 / RELATION 3: Route cumulative cost. Formula C_total=sum_i(C_material_i+C_process_i). Dimensional condition: All costs in same declared currency per candidate batch. Predicted geometric signature: Budget-feasibility plateau. Rival: Disposal and safety costs omitted from reported cost.. F135 / RELATION 4: Precursor availability ratio. Formula A=100*N_available/N_required. Dimensional condition: Counts in stock catalogue; availability percent. Predicted geometric signature: Stockout singular boundary. Rival: A public catalogue listing is not proof of legal local availability.. F135 / RELATION 5: Cycle-free route indicator. Formula DAG=I[retrosynthetic_route_is_acyclic]. Dimensional condition: Binary graph-theoretic condition, dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Graph-cycle fault manifold. Rival: Acyclic route still may be chemically impossible.. F135 / RELATION 6: Expert validation agreement. Formula Kappa=(p_o-p_e)/(1-p_e). Dimensional condition: Observed and chance agreement dimensionless; kappa dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Expert disagreement saddle. Rival: High consensus does not ensure true practical syntheses.. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

Formula N=100*N_novel_scaffolds/N_valid. Dimensional condition: Novel scaffold count divided by valid generated count, percent. Formula J=log(p_graph)-lambda*P_invalid. Dimensional condition: Log probability and penalty dimensionless, lambda dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Feasible manifold under valence penalties. Rival: Reward hacking can improve J while molecular chemistry degrades.. F131 / RELATION 5: Shannon graph diversity. Formula H=-sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Dimensional condition: p_i relative graph frequencies; entropy nats. Predicted geometric signature: Diversity ridge subject to sampling noise. Rival: A high-entropy distribution can be mostly chemically invalid.. F131 / RELATION 6: Held-out validity difference. Formula DeltaV=V_model-V_classical. Dimensional condition: Both V in percent; DeltaV percentage points. Predicted geometric signature: External scaffold frontier can invert an internal advantage. Rival: A strong classic fragment generator may beat the proposed model.. F132 / RELATION 1: Blind attribute correlation. Formula r=cov(yhat,y)/(sd(yhat)*sd(y)). Rival: Repeated ratings or leaked descriptors can inflate correlation.. F132 / RELATION 2: Correlation Fisher transform. Formula z=0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)). Dimensional condition: Predictions and ratings in same registered rating-scale units. Predicted geometric signature: Error valley across label calibration. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

Formula J=log(p_graph)-lambda*P_invalid. Dimensional condition: Log probability and penalty dimensionless, lambda dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Feasible manifold under valence penalties. Rival: Reward hacking can improve J while molecular chemistry degrades.. F131 / RELATION 5: Shannon graph diversity. Formula H=-sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Dimensional condition: p_i relative graph frequencies; entropy nats. Predicted geometric signature: Diversity ridge subject to sampling noise. Rival: A high-entropy distribution can be mostly chemically invalid.. F131 / RELATION 6: Held-out validity difference. Formula DeltaV=V_model-V_classical. Dimensional condition: Both V in percent; DeltaV percentage points. Predicted geometric signature: External scaffold frontier can invert an internal advantage. Rival: A strong classic fragment generator may beat the proposed model.. F132 / RELATION 1: Blind attribute correlation. Formula r=cov(yhat,y)/(sd(yhat)*sd(y)). Dimensional condition: Standard deviation and covariance matched scale; r dimensionless from -1 to 1. Predicted geometric signature: Correlation saddle under rater reliability and scaffold shift. Rival: Repeated ratings or leaked descriptors can inflate correlation.. F132 / RELATION 2: Correlation Fisher transform. Formula z=0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)). Dimensional condition: r dimensionless -1<r<1; z dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Exploding endpoints near perfect correlation. Rival: High z is unstable for small or dependent test sets.. F132 / RELATION 3: Attribute MAE. Formula MAE=(1/N)*sum|yhat_i-y_i|. Dimensional condition: Predictions and ratings in same registered rating-scale units. Predicted geometric signature: Error valley across label calibration. Rival: A changed rater scale can fabricate gains.. F132 / RELATION 4: Hierarchical rater variance. Formula u_total2=u_molecule2+u_rater2+u_lab2. Dimensional condition: All variances in squared descriptor rating units. Predicted geometric signature: Uncertainty floor across cohorts. Rival: Ignoring correlated raters invalidates independence.. F132 / RELATION 5: Rank-based agreement. Formula rho=1-6*sum_i d_i^2/(N*(N^2-1)). Dimensional condition: Spearman rho dimensionless for uncensored tie-free ranks. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

Formula N=100*N_novel_scaffolds/N_valid. Dimensional condition: Novel scaffold count divided by valid generated count, percent. Formula J=log(p_graph)-lambda*P_invalid. Dimensional condition: Log probability and penalty dimensionless, lambda dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Feasible manifold under valence penalties. Rival: Reward hacking can improve J while molecular chemistry degrades.. F131 / RELATION 5: Shannon graph diversity. Formula H=-sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Dimensional condition: p_i relative graph frequencies; entropy nats. Predicted geometric signature: Diversity ridge subject to sampling noise. Rival: A high-entropy distribution can be mostly chemically invalid.. F131 / RELATION 6: Held-out validity difference. Formula DeltaV=V_model-V_classical. Rival: A strong classic fragment generator may beat the proposed model.. F132 / RELATION 1: Blind attribute correlation. Formula r=cov(yhat,y)/(sd(yhat)*sd(y)). Rival: High z is unstable for small or dependent test sets.. F132 / RELATION 3: Attribute MAE. Formula MAE=(1/N)*sum|yhat_i-y_i|. Dimensional condition: Predictions and ratings in same registered rating-scale units. Predicted geometric signature: Error valley across label calibration. Rival: A changed rater scale can fabricate gains.. F132 / RELATION 4: Hierarchical rater variance. Formula u_total2=u_molecule2+u_rater2+u_lab2. Dimensional condition: All variances in squared descriptor rating units. Predicted geometric signature: Uncertainty floor across cohorts. Rival: Ignoring correlated raters invalidates independence.. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: This replication package accompanies the study of Norgespris, Norway's voluntary fixed-price electricity scheme. The paper compares electricity meters that entered the scheme early with meters classified as non-adopters in three southern Norwegian bidding zones (NO1, NO2 and NO5) from October 2023 to April 2026. It examines who stood to gain from fixed-price protection, how the cohorts responded to daily electricity prices before and after adoption, and how their relative consumption changed. The archive includes aggregate hourly consumption and meter counts from Elhub, ERA5 temperature data obtained through Open-Meteo, and the Python and R code used to generate the tables, figures and numerical results in the paper and its supplement. The README gives the software versions, the command for running the analysis, and a guide to the files behind each exhibit. The included retrieval script obtains the hourly electricity prices from Hva koster strømmen and checks all 2,829 supplier responses against their archived SHA-256 digests.
title: Who Gives Up the Price Signal? Selection, Price Responsiveness and Demand under Norway's Voluntary Fixed Electricity Price
